113| \begin{solution}{exo:b3:microcanonical-ensemble:12}
114| (a) $v = (\qty{550}{nm})^3 = \qty{1.7e-19}{m^3}$: $\bar n =
115| \num{4.2e6}$, $\delta_{\text{rms}} = 1/\sqrt{\bar n} \approx
116| \num{5e-4}$. (b) A perfectly uniform medium would scatter nothing
117| sideways (\cref{pb:b3:perturbation-theory:1}, Part III): these
118| irreducible $\sqrt N$ ripples in every optical cell are precisely
119| the disorder that lets the sky exist. (c) $\bar n = 100$: $v
120| \approx (\qty{16}{nm})^3$. (d) The sky is blue because air is made
121| of countable molecules whose numbers fluctuate as $\sqrt N$ ---
122| Einstein used exactly this to argue molecules were real.
123| \end{solution}

125| \begin{solution}{pb:b3:microcanonical-ensemble:1}
126| \textbf{1.} $n_\pm = \tfrac12(N \pm x/b)$; $\Omega =
127| N!/n_+!\,n_-!$.
128| \textbf{2.} At $x = 0$: the free chain coils; full extension has
129| $\Omega = 1$.
130| \textbf{3.} Stirling on the binomial, expanded to second order in
131| $x/Nb$: the stated Gaussian entropy.
132| \textbf{4.} With $E$ independent of $x$, any pull toward small
133| $x$ can only come from the count: entropic by construction.
134| \textbf{5.} Coil $\sim b\sqrt N = \qty{50}{nm}$ against $Nb =
135| \qty{5}{\micro m}$: the free chain is a hundred times shorter
136| than its contour --- crumpled almost entirely.
137| \textbf{6.} $N$, the number of links between cross-links:
138| vulcanisation shortens the effective chains, stiffening the
139| network.
140| \textbf{7.} $f = -T\,\partial S/\partial x =
141| k_{\text{B}}Tx/Nb^2$.
142| \textbf{8.} $k = k_{\text{B}}T/Nb^2 = \num{4.14e-21}/(\num{e4}
143| \times \num{2.5e-19}) = \qty{1.7e-6}{N/m}$ per chain.
144| \textbf{9.} $k \propto T$: heated under fixed load, the band
145| stiffens and \emph{contracts}, lifting the load; a steel spring
146| merely softens and sags a little.
147| \textbf{10.} $f(Nb/2) = k_{\text{B}}T/2b \approx \qty{4}{pN}$;
148| the linear law fails as $f$ approaches $k_{\text{B}}T/b \approx
149| \qty{8}{pN}$, where the chain nears full extension.
150| \textbf{11.} $\sim\num{e14}$ chains in parallel and
151| $\sim\num{e5}$ coil-lengths in series along a centimetre:
152| $k_{\text{band}} \sim k_{\text{chain}} \times \num{e14}/\num{e5}
153| \sim \num{e2}$--$\num{e3}\,\unit{N/m}$ --- the familiar feel of a
154| rubber band.
155| \textbf{12.} Rubber's stiffness \emph{is} $k_{\text{B}}T$ per
156| configuration: more agitation, more recoil; metallic stiffness is
157| bond energy, which anharmonic agitation loosens.
158| \textbf{13.} Stretching cuts the configurational count; done fast
159| (no entropy exchanged with outside), the lost configurational
160| entropy must reappear as thermal entropy: the band warms ---
161| \qty{1}{K}-scale, lip-detectable.
162| \textbf{14.} Releasing restores configurations; the thermal
163| account refunds the difference: it cools.
164| \textbf{15.} The weight \emph{rises}: contraction on heating is
165| the entropic signature (energy-elastic materials expand).
166| \textbf{16.} The steel spring lengthens slightly (thermal
167| expansion) and its modulus drops: opposite sign --- elasticity of
168| energy, not of counting.
169| \textbf{17.} Heated spokes contract, pulling the rim's mass
170| off-centre toward the cool side; gravity torques the unbalanced
171| wheel; each spoke re-relaxes as it rotates away: a heat engine
172| whose working substance is entropy itself.
173| \textbf{18.} $k_{\text{B}}T/b = \num{4.14e-21}/\num{e-7} =
174| \qty{4e-14}{N} = \qty{0.04}{pN}$: piconewtons and below ---
175| exactly the optical-tweezer range, so the force--extension law of
176| one DNA molecule could be traced point by point (and matched,
177| with the refinements of item 23).
178| \textbf{19.} From nowhere but the count: at extension $x$ there
179| are fewer microstates than at $x - \dd x$, and thermal agitation
180| drifts the chain toward the bigger count; the ``force'' is
181| $T$ times the entropy gradient.
182| \textbf{20.} At $T = 0$ nothing explores configurations: the
183| entropic force vanishes with the agitation that powers it ---
184| elasticity would be purely energetic, and rubber would behave
185| like a limp thread.
186| \textbf{21.} Gas: $P = T\,\partial S/\partial V$ with $S \ni
187| Nk_{\text{B}}\ln V$; chain: $f = -T\,\partial S/\partial x$ with
188| the Gaussian count --- both are counting pushed against a
189| constraint, priced at $T$.
190| \textbf{22.} The dryer's heat enters the band; part is converted
191| to work in the isothermal contraction, the books balanced by the
192| entropy carried in and out --- a miniature heat engine, first law
193| intact.
194| \textbf{23.} Finite extensibility (the real force diverges near
195| full stretch --- the worm-like-chain refinement) and
196| strain-induced crystallisation (alignment orders the chains,
197| giving hysteresis and heat release beyond the ideal model).
198| \textbf{24.} $k_{\text{B}}T/\unit{nm} = \qty{4.1}{pN}$: the
199| force at which thermal energy and nanometre displacements trade
200| evenly --- molecular motors, folding proteins and stretched DNA
201| all operate within an order of magnitude of it.
202| \textbf{25.} Ten thousand blind links, counted: Hooke's law with
203| $k = k_{\text{B}}T/Nb^2$, warmth on stretching, weights lifted by
204| hot air, and single molecules obeying at \qty{0.04}{pN} ---
205| entropy, acting as a force.
206| \end{solution}
